issues.legal_issue: The agricultural-land ceiling scheme permits a holder to acquire land only up to the applicable ceiling and makes any excess holding liable to surrender.
material_facts: The legislation imposed a maximum limit on agricultural-land holdings and provided for acquisition and distribution of land held in excess of that limit.
The court considered the statutory restriction on acquiring land where the holder’s existing land, together with the proposed acquisition, would exceed the ceiling.
issues.conclusion: A person or family unit may acquire land only up to the ceiling limit; land held in excess of the limit is liable to be surrendered under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 5 establish the prohibition on holdings beyond the ceiling and the ceiling area, while Section 9 bars an acquisition that would cause the holder’s total holding to exceed that area. The Act’s purpose is to acquire and distribute land held in excess of the ceiling. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.agricultural_land_ceiling_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the application of a statutory ceiling on agricultural-land holdings.
predicates.existing_holding_at_or_below_ceiling: The person or family unit holds no more land than the applicable ceiling before the proposed acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_would_exceed_ceiling: The proposed acquisition would cause the total holding to exceed the applicable ceiling.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding concerns a holder whose existing holding is within the limit, an acquisition that would take the total beyond the limit makes the excess holding liable to surrender.

issues.legal_issue: A finding that a person or family unit holds less than the ceiling is not an appealable declaration, and an appeal not authorized by law does not bar supervisory revision.
material_facts: The Collector found that the holder was below the applicable ceiling and made no declaration of surplus land under Section 21.
The holder nevertheless appealed, seeking a finding that his holding was smaller; the appeal was summarily dismissed.
The Commissioner later initiated revision of the Collector’s proceedings and determined that the holding exceeded the ceiling.
issues.conclusion: The Collector’s finding was not appealable; the appeal was not one provided by law and therefore did not prevent the exercise of revisional power.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14 to 20 provide for inquiry and determination, while Section 21 requires a declaration in a surplus-holder case. Section 33 provides an appeal against specified orders and a Section 21 declaration or part thereof, not against a mere finding that a holding is below the ceiling. Section 45(2) provides supervisory revision, subject to its proviso concerning an appeal against a Section 21 declaration. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.ceiling_act_revision_proceeding: The proceeding concerns supervisory revision of an agricultural-land ceiling determination.
predicates.no_surplus_declaration_made: The original decision found the holding below the ceiling and made no declaration of surplus land.
predicates.appeal_challenges_below_ceiling_finding: An appeal was filed against the finding that the holding was below the ceiling, rather than against a surplus declaration.

issues.definition: In a ceiling revision proceeding, when no surplus declaration was made and the appeal challenged only a below-ceiling finding, the unauthorized appeal does not bar revision.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier determination of a landholding may not preclude a later surplus determination when that later proceeding concerns land acquired afterward, although the earlier determination remains relevant.
material_facts: The court considered the possibility of later proceedings to determine surplus land after acquisition of additional land.
An earlier proceeding had determined the holder’s landholding at a particular figure.
issues.conclusion: The earlier determination may not operate as res judicata in the later proceeding, though it remains relevant; the court did not make a definitive determination of the point.
issues.legal_principle: The court observed that a determination of the extent of a holding is an intermediate step toward the Act’s purpose and is not a determination or declaration of title. It stated that an earlier determination may not operate as res judicata in subsequent proceedings concerning surplus land, while remaining relevant. Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure concerns res judicata; no earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.later_surplus_determination_proceeding: The proceeding seeks to determine surplus land after an earlier holding determination.
predicates.earlier_holding_determination: An earlier proceeding determined the extent of the person’s or family unit’s holding.
predicates.later_proceeding_considers_later_acquire: The later proceeding considers land acquired after the earlier determination.

issues.definition: When a later surplus determination considers later-acquired land, an earlier holding determination is not necessarily preclusive, though it remains relevant.

issues.legal_issue: Land received under a disbelieved exchange must be excluded from the holder’s landholding when the land given in the exchange is also included and no other means of acquiring the received land is claimed.
material_facts: The holder claimed that land he owned had been exchanged for a larger parcel belonging to another person.
The Commissioner disbelieved the claimed exchange but included both the land given and the land received in the holder’s total holding.
No one claimed that the holder had acquired the received parcel by any means other than the alleged exchange.
issues.conclusion: The parcel received under the alleged exchange had to be excluded from the holding when the exchange was disbelieved and the parcel given was also included.
issues.legal_principle: In reviewing the surplus determination under Section 45, the court held that, on these facts, including both parcels was unjustified: once the alleged exchange was disbelieved and the land given remained included, the land received could not also be included where no other acquisition was alleged. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: agricultural_land_ceiling_determination_proceeding and alleged_exchange_disbelieved and land_given_in_exchange_included and no_alternative_acquisition_claimed

predicates.agricultural_land_ceiling_determination_: The proceeding determines a person’s holding for purposes of an agricultural-land ceiling.
predicates.alleged_exchange_disbelieved: The decision-maker rejects the claimed exchange as the means by which the holder acquired the disputed parcel.
predicates.land_given_in_exchange_included: The land claimed to have been given in the exchange remains included in the holder’s total holding.
predicates.no_alternative_acquisition_claimed: No party claims that the holder acquired the received parcel by a means other than the alleged exchange.

issues.definition: In a ceiling determination, if the exchange is disbelieved, the land given remains included, and no alternative acquisition is claimed, the land received under the exchange is excluded.
